message.content:
Read-only survey of the Callisto repo at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/verify-manifest-findings (Rust release tool; see ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/architecture/*.md, docs/adr/*.md).

Context: we are considering a pattern where, before a command makes local changes, it snapshots the pre-run working-tree state as a git commit pointed to by a ref (refs/callisto/...), deletes the ref on success, and on failure uses the ref to resume (re-derive the same work from the exact pre-run state) or abort (git restore from the ref). It is being designed first for `callisto version`, whose apply writes manifests, changelogs and pre.json, refreshes lockfiles with external tools, stages, then consumes changesets.

Question: which OTHER commands or code paths in Callisto have the same shape — several local file or git-index changes plus a fallible step (external tool, network, git) where a failure midway leaves a half-changed state, or where the code already does its own snapshot/restore/temporary-change-then-undo, interrupted-run detection, or retry guard? Consider at least: snapshot (ApplyOptions::transient), pre enter/exit, init, add, release (local), release-pr / release PR branch creation, compose-pr-body, generated-workflow writes, anything that creates branches, tags, or commits, and anything that temporarily edits manifests and restores them.

For each site report: file:line, what it changes, what can fail after the changes, what happens today on failure (cite the code), and whether a pre-run git snapshot ref would simplify or fix it, or would not fit (e.g. remote effects like registry publishes or pushed tags, which ADR 3 handles by adoption). Also note any existing use of custom git refs, git stash, temporary indexes (GIT_INDEX_FILE), or git worktrees in the code. Keep the report to what you verified in the code; mark anything inferred. Under 600 words.

Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# The version command consumes the changesets the body describes, so it also writes the facts the body is built from.
preview_file=$(mktemp)
read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
command+=(--emit-decision "$INPUT_DECISION_PATH" --emit-preview "$preview_file")
"${command[@]}"

if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh_retry pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  report=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --preview "$preview_file" --publish-plan --existing-body - --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format json)
else
  report=$(callisto compose-pr-body --preview "$preview_file" --publish-plan --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format json)
fi
rm -f "$preview_file"
body=$(jq -r '.body' <<< "$report")
# Callisto owns the label catalog: each entry says whether it belongs on the PR now, so nothing here names a label.
applied_labels=()
while IFS= read -r name; do applied_labels+=("$name"); done < <(jq -r '.labels[]? | select(.applied) | .name' <<< "$report")
unapplied_labels=()
while IFS= read -r name; do unapplied_labels+=("$name"); done < <(jq -r '.labels[]? | select(.applied | not) | .name' <<< "$report")
git add -A
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }

plan_file=$(mktemp)

All paths are under /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/verify-manifest-findings. I read only.

**Existing refs, stash, temporary indexes and worktrees**
- The only use is the uncommitted spike in `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs`. `git status` shows it as modified.
  - It uses `refs/callisto/version-base` (:148), a temporary index through `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (:150-179), `commit-tree` plus `update-ref` (:164-181), and `worktree add --detach` / `worktree remove --force` for resume (:43, :99).
  - Line 172 runs `git :/ add -A`, which is malformed. Its result is ignored.
  - `.expect()` calls panic on any git failure.
  - A resume plans from the base ref but applies to the real tree, and nothing restores it on abort.
- The committed code uses no stash, no `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, no worktree and no custom ref. The only match is `env_remove("GIT_INDEX_FILE")` in a test helper at `callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:1166`.
- I found no code that edits a manifest temporarily and then restores it. Searches for restore/rollback/allow-dirty in the release and publish code found nothing.

**Retry guards that already exist for `version` (committed code)**
- `apply.rs:461` `write_version_guarded`: skips a manifest that already has the target version and refuses one that has neither the old nor the new version.
- `commands/version.rs:518`: raises `PartialVersionRun` (E121, `error.rs:244-262`) when disk, index and HEAD disagree.
- `apply.rs:241-279`: stages everything first. Changesets and pre.json are removed from disk only after `git rm --cached` succeeds.
- `apply/preflight.rs:93` checks writability and ignored paths before the first write.
- The resume ref would replace E121 and the from/to guard. It would not replace the ordering.

**Other sites, one by one**

1. **snapshot** (`commands/snapshot.rs:26-32`, `apply.rs` with `transient: true`)
   - Changes: manifests, plus lockfile refresh through external tools. Nothing is staged and there are no changelogs or changeset removal (`apply.rs:168, 236, 241`).
   - Can fail: `cargo update` and similar tools after the manifests are written.
   - Today: the error propagates and the tree is left half-written, with no cleanup.
   - Fit: a snapshot ref fits for abort, since `git restore` would undo it. Resume is less useful because the change is meant to be throwaway. (Inferred: snapshot runs in CI on a disposable checkout.)

2. **pre enter / pre exit** (`commands/pre.rs:129-133`, `:186-189`)
   - Changes: an atomic write of pre.json, then `git add`.
   - Can fail: `git add`. The file is then changed but not staged.
   - Today: the error is returned. Re-running `enter` fails with `PreAlreadyActive` (:101) and `exit` with `PreAlreadyExited` (:167), so the user has to stage by hand.
   - Fit: it would work, but a ref is too much for one file. Making the command idempotent when pre.json already says the target state would be simpler.

3. **init** (`cli/commands/init.rs:263-269`; `graph/commands/init.rs:538-558`, `:930`)
   - Changes: writes callisto.toml, then `.changeset/README.md`, then the workflow.
   - Can fail: the network/git step (`ls-remote` in `resolve_release_commit`, :826) runs in `build_workflow` before any write, so that is safe. Only local I/O can fail between the writes.
   - Today: a re-run is blocked by `ensure_uninitialized` (:168, E: InitAlreadyInitialized) and by `ensure_workflow_absent` (:917). There is no cleanup.
   - Fit: weak, because the fallible step comes before the writes. Inferred: init often runs in a repo with no commits (`facts.has_commit`), where a ref has no HEAD to point at.

4. **add** (`commands/add.rs:262-290`)
   - Changes: one `atomic_write_new` with a retry on slug collision.
   - Fit: does not need one.

5. **release (local)** (`release/local.rs:26-28`, `vcs/access.rs:384`)
   - It requires a clean worktree and writes nothing to tracked files.
   - The tag provider (`release/provider/tag.rs:55-82`) creates a local tag only if it is absent, then pushes it. The comment says a run whose push failed leaves "exactly as prepared ... only the push remains".
   - Registry and forge effects are adopted on re-run (ADR 0003).
   - Fit: does not fit. The local tag is already idempotent.

6. **release-pr** (`commands/release_pr.rs:1-5`)
   - `decide`/`verify`/`commit-plan` read the index and worktree and write only `--out` files.
   - Branch creation is in `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh`. That script runs `callisto version` (:98-101), `compose-pr-body` (:104-107) and `git add -A` (:117), and never commits locally (:8).
   - Remote changes go through a staging branch: reset or create it (:139-149), call `createCommitOnBranch` with retry and reset (:172-173), then delete it in `trap cleanup_staging EXIT` (:125-132).
   - Fit: this is remote, disposable CI state. A local ref adds nothing. It already has its own staging-ref pattern on the remote side.

7. **compose-pr-body** (`commands/compose_pr_body.rs`)
   - It is read-only and prints to stdout.
   - Fit: none needed.

8. **The version tail** (`cli/commands/version.rs:112-126`)
   - Changes: `--emit-decision` and `--emit-preview` are written after apply has consumed the changesets.
   - Can fail: either write.
   - Today: the write fails after apply has already finished, and the decision can no longer be derived from the changesets.
   - Fit: good. The base ref should stay in place until these writes succeed. The spike deletes it at :105, which is before these writes, so this is a gap.

9. **`.github/scripts/move-floating-tag.sh:40-48`**
   - It force-fetches, force-tags and force-pushes a remote tag.
   - Fit: does not fit (remote).

**Generated workflow writes**
- Apart from `init`'s `write_workflow` (site 3), I found no other code that writes a workflow file.

- `apply.rs:241-279`: stages everything first. Changesets and pre.json are removed from disk only after `git rm --cached` succeeds.
- `apply/preflight.rs:93` checks writability and ignored paths before the first write.
- The resume ref would replace E121 and the from/to guard. It would not replace the ordering.

**Other sites, one by one**

1. **snapshot** (`commands/snapshot.rs:26-32`, `apply.rs` with `transient: true`)
   - Changes: manifests, plus lockfile refresh through external tools. Nothing is staged and there are no changelogs or changeset removal (`apply.rs:168, 236, 241`).
   - Can fail: `cargo update` and similar tools after the manifests are written.
   - Today: the error propagates and the tree is left half-written, with no cleanup.
   - Fit: a snapshot ref fits for abort, since `git restore` would undo it. Resume is less useful because the change is meant to be throwaway. (Inferred: snapshot runs in CI on a disposable checkout.)

2. **pre enter / pre exit** (`commands/pre.rs:129-133`, `:186-189`)
   - Changes: an atomic write of pre.json, then `git add`.
   - Can fail: `git add`. The file is then changed but not staged.
   - Today: the error is returned. Re-running `enter` fails with `PreAlreadyActive` (:101) and `exit` with `PreAlreadyExited` (:167), so the user has to stage by hand.
   - Fit: it would work, but a ref is too much for one file. Making the command idempotent when pre.json already says the target state would be simpler.

3. **init** (`cli/commands/init.rs:263-269`; `graph/commands/init.rs:538-558`, `:930`)
   - Changes: writes callisto.toml, then `.changeset/README.md`, then the workflow.
   - Can fail: the network/git step (`ls-remote` in `resolve_release_commit`, :826) runs in `build_workflow` before any write, so that is safe. Only local I/O can fail between the writes.
   - Today: a re-run is blocked by `ensure_uninitialized` (:168, E: InitAlreadyInitialized) and by `ensure_workflow_absent` (:917). There is no cleanup.
   - Fit: weak, because the fallible step comes before the writes. Inferred: init often runs in a repo with no commits (`facts.has_commit`), where a ref has no HEAD to point at.

4. **add** (`commands/add.rs:262-290`)
   - Changes: one `atomic_write_new` with a retry on slug collision.
   - Fit: does not need one.

5. **release (local)** (`release/local.rs:26-28`, `vcs/access.rs:384`)
   - It requires a clean worktree and writes nothing to tracked files.
   - The tag provider (`release/provider/tag.rs:55-82`) creates a local tag only if it is absent, then pushes it. The comment says a run whose push failed leaves "exactly as prepared ... only the push remains".
   - Registry and forge effects are adopted on re-run (ADR 0003).
   - Fit: does not fit. The local tag is already idempotent.

6. **release-pr** (`commands/release_pr.rs:1-5`)
   - `decide`/`verify`/`commit-plan` read the index and worktree and write only `--out` files.
   - Branch creation is in `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh`. That script runs `callisto version` (:98-101), `compose-pr-body` (:104-107) and `git add -A` (:117), and never commits locally (:8).
   - Remote changes go through a staging branch: reset or create it (:139-149), call `createCommitOnBranch` with retry and reset (:172-173), then delete it in `trap cleanup_staging EXIT` (:125-132).
   - Fit: this is remote, disposable CI state. A local ref adds nothing. It already has its own staging-ref pattern on the remote side.

7. **compose-pr-body** (`commands/compose_pr_body.rs`)
   - It is read-only and prints to stdout.
   - Fit: none needed.

8. **The version tail** (`cli/commands/version.rs:112-126`)
   - Changes: `--emit-decision` and `--emit-preview` are written after apply has consumed the changesets.
   - Can fail: either write.
   - Today: the write fails after apply has already finished, and the decision can no longer be derived from the changesets.
   - Fit: good. The base ref should stay in place until these writes succeed. The spike deletes it at :105, which is before these writes, so this is a gap.

9. **`.github/scripts/move-floating-tag.sh:40-48`**
   - It force-fetches, force-tags and force-pushes a remote tag.
   - Fit: does not fit (remote).

**Generated workflow writes**
- Apart from `init`'s `write_workflow` (site 3), I found no other code that writes a workflow file.
